name: Plaque – Generalised
description: Soft microbial deposit present on most tooth surfaces; indicator of poor oral hygiene.

name: Calculus – Supragingival
description: Mineralised deposits above the gumline, visible on clinical examination.

name: Calculus – Subgingival
description: Mineralised deposits below the gumline; detected by probing or radiograph.

name: Gingival Bleeding on Probing
description: Bleeding upon gentle probing; indicates active gingival or periodontal inflammation.

name: Gingival Recession
description: Apical migration of the gingival margin exposing root surface.

name: Gingival Enlargement / Hyperplasia
description: Excessive gingival tissue; may be drug-induced, inflammatory, or fibrous.

name: Periodontal Pocket 3–4 mm
description: Mild pocket depth indicating early attachment loss.

name: Periodontal Pocket 5–6 mm
description: Moderate pocket depth requiring deep scaling or periodontal surgery.

name: Periodontal Pocket ≥ 7 mm
description: Severe pocket depth associated with significant bone loss.

name: Caries – Cavitation Present
description: Visible cavity or breakdown of tooth structure due to decay.

name: Caries – Early (White Spot Lesion)
description: Initial demineralisation appearing as an opaque white spot; reversible with fluoride.

name: Fractured Tooth / Cracked Tooth Syndrome
description: Incomplete or complete fracture of tooth structure, with or without pulp exposure.

name: Worn / Flat Occlusal Surface
description: Attrition of the chewing surface, often associated with bruxism.

name: Defective / Fractured Existing Restoration
description: Failed filling or crown with marginal gaps, fracture, or secondary caries.

name: Tooth Mobility – Grade I (0.5–1 mm)
description: Slight horizontal mobility; early sign of periodontal or occlusal involvement.

name: Tooth Mobility – Grade II (1–2 mm)
description: Moderate horizontal mobility with no vertical movement.

name: Tooth Mobility – Grade III (>2 mm or vertical)
description: Severe mobility in all directions; tooth often non-restorable.

name: Localised Swelling / Fluctuant Swelling
description: Soft-tissue swelling indicating abscess or infection requiring drainage.

name: Sinus Tract (Parulis)
description: Pus-draining fistula from a chronic periapical or periodontal infection.

name: Soft-Tissue Impaction – Third Molar
description: Wisdom tooth partially covered by operculum, predisposing to pericoronitis.

name: Exposed Root Surface
description: Visible root due to gingival recession; may be sensitive and caries-prone.

name: Class I Molar Relationship
description: Mesio-buccal cusp of upper first molar occludes in the buccal groove of lower first molar.

name: Class II Molar Relationship
description: Lower arch is distal relative to upper; associated with overjet.

name: Class III Molar Relationship
description: Lower arch is mesial relative to upper; associated with underbite.

name: Mild Crowding
description: Slight arch-length discrepancy with minor tooth rotation or displacement.

name: Moderate to Severe Crowding
description: Significant arch-length deficiency requiring orthodontic or surgical intervention.

name: Spacing / Diastema
description: Gaps between teeth, including midline diastema; orthodontic or restorative treatment.

name: Extrinsic Staining
description: Surface stains from tea, coffee, tobacco, or chromogenic bacteria; removed by polishing.

name: Intrinsic Discolouration
description: Internal tooth discolouration from fluorosis, tetracycline, trauma, or pulp necrosis.

name: Attrition (Tooth-to-Tooth Wear)
description: Flattened occlusal/incisal surfaces from tooth-on-tooth contact, often bruxism-related.

name: Abrasion (Mechanical Wear)
description: Notched or wedge-shaped cervical tooth loss from mechanical causes such as aggressive brushing.

name: Abfraction Lesion
description: Wedge-shaped cervical defect attributed to occlusal flexural stress.

name: Sensitivity to Percussion
description: Pain on tapping the tooth; suggests periapical or periodontal ligament inflammation.

name: Positive Cold Test (Lingering Pain)
description: Prolonged pain response to cold stimulus; indicates irreversible pulpal involvement.

name: Negative Pulp Vitality Response
description: No response to thermal/electric pulp testing; suggests pulp necrosis.

name: Internal Root Resorption (Radiographic)
description: Balloon-shaped radiolucency within the root canal space seen on radiograph.

name: External Root Resorption (Radiographic)
description: Irregular root surface loss visible radiographically, often trauma- or pressure-related.

name: Periapical Radiolucency
description: Radiographic lucency at the root apex indicating periapical pathology.

name: Widened Periodontal Ligament Space
description: Radiographic widening of the PDL space, suggestive of occlusal trauma or early periapical change.

name: Furcation Involvement – Grade I
description: Incipient furcation involvement detectable by probe but less than 3mm horizontally.

name: Furcation Involvement – Grade II
description: Cul-de-sac furcation involvement extending more than 3mm but not through-and-through.

name: Furcation Involvement – Grade III
description: Through-and-through furcation involvement; probe passes completely under the tooth.

name: Horizontal Bone Loss (Radiographic)
description: Even reduction in alveolar bone height parallel to the CEJ line, seen radiographically.

name: Vertical (Angular) Bone Loss (Radiographic)
description: Localised angular bone defect, often associated with isolated periodontal pockets.

name: TMJ Clicking / Crepitus
description: Audible or palpable joint sound on opening/closing; suggests disc displacement or degenerative change.

name: Deviation on Mouth Opening
description: Jaw shifts to one side during opening, indicating asymmetric TMJ or muscle function.

name: Masticatory Muscle Tenderness on Palpation
description: Pain on palpation of masseter/temporalis; suggests myofascial involvement or bruxism.

name: Root Fracture (Radiographic)
description: Radiolucent line across the root visible on radiograph, typically trauma-related.

name: Tooth Luxation / Displacement
description: Tooth displaced from its socket following trauma; may be extruded, intruded, or laterally displaced.

name: Xerostomia (Dry Mouth)
description: Reduced salivary flow presenting as dryness; increases caries and mucosal risk.

name: Halitosis
description: Persistent oral malodour, often linked to periodontal disease, coating, or systemic causes.

name: Tongue Coating
description: Visible white/yellow coating on dorsal tongue surface, associated with poor hygiene or halitosis.

name: Impacted / Ectopic Supernumerary Tooth
description: Extra tooth present in an abnormal position, often detected radiographically.
